prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a rare case where a specific theoretical prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) told experimentalists where to look, and nature then delivered more than was asked: correlated insulators and superconductivity in a carbon system (Jarillo-Herrero's group, 2018). The result has been reproduced by many independent groups using transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, and the single-particle band picture is quantitatively understood, which is the kind of theory-measurement link I trust. It has created a tunable platform that has spread to twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides and to fractional Chern insulator physics. It also echoes the lesson of 2010, when experiment overturned what theorists thought they knew about two-dimensional crystals. A single-achievement prize with a theory pair and the experimental discoverer gives a clean and defensible citation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity: eight years after the experiments, the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated, and sample and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility. The citation therefore has to be framed around the observed phases and the flat-band prediction, not the mechanism. Attribution is also imperfect: Yuan Cao as first author, Dean, Kim, Young, Efetov and others, and the earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto work all have claims that a three-person limit cannot fully meet. If the committee judges the field too young, B042 is the better-settled discovery in my view, and B058 is the more mature condensed-matter candidate.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked KPZ universality first for its simple general mechanism and rated twisted bilayer graphene second, noting that the superconducting pairing is unsettled, that timing is arguably early, and that Cao and the wider community complicate a three-person split.
responses.response: I share the maturity concern and think it is the right test. I would answer it by separating the discovery of the phases, which is robust and widely reproduced, from their explanation, which is not, and the prize should reward only the first. I also value your point about simple general mechanisms: interference of two lattices with a small twist is exactly that, and it has proved far more generative than KPZ has been outside statistical physics. I defer to you on KPZ itself. My question is whether the credit chain there (Kardar and Zhang for the equation, Takeuchi for the experiment, with the exact-solution community left out) is as thin as your own attribution note suggests. I do not think B037 is the stronger configuration, but I would like to hear more on that.

responses.point: Olsson ranked aberration-corrected electron microscopy first as a verified invention that lets us see what could not be seen before, and placed twisted bilayer graphene and tunnel magnetoresistance next, while flagging the missing Krivanek and the physics-versus-instrument question.
responses.response: I rank B028 low, but not for lack of impact. Aberration-corrected microscopy is the instrument against which much of my own field tests its electronic-structure calculations, and I agree it is fully mature. My reservation is the attribution gap you identify. A prize that omits Krivanek and the STEM corrector line is hard to defend, and the three credited names cannot cover both TEM and STEM correctors. I do agree with you on B058: tunnel magnetoresistance is a strong second choice for me, and I take your point that the MgO step is shared with Yuasa and Djayaprawira. Where we differ is that I put the flat-band discovery ahead because it revealed new quantum states, whereas B028 is an enabling instrument, which Nobel's will does permit but which I weigh below a new phase of matter.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first because magic-wavelength trapping turned thousands of atoms into a quantum-limited oscillator, with 1e-18 uncertainty, independent confirmation across many laboratories and a clean Katori-Ye split, while asking whether it is distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I agree B042 has the cleanest attribution and the strongest independent confirmation on the table. Those are exactly the qualities I would look for. My difference is one of kind: lattice clocks are an extraordinary refinement of a measurement capability that earlier prizes already opened, while twisted bilayer graphene revealed new matter. I do not regard the 2005 and 2012 overlap as disqualifying, since the magic-wavelength idea is a distinct conceptual step. If the committee prefers the better-settled candidate, I would support B042 and would not treat that as a poor outcome. I would ask you and Lindroth whether the Ye comb and cavity-stabilisation work is separable from the 2005 prize for the purposes of a fair citation.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked optical lattice clocks first as the cleanest case for quantitative agreement between theory and experiment, ranked ultracold-atom lattices second, and noted that Zoller appears in both the lattice and trapped-ion candidates so one set of theorists should not be rewarded twice.
responses.response: I agree with your point about Zoller: B050 and B038 should be treated as competing configurations, and the committee should not split credit across them. For that reason I would not pair B050 with B019 even though it is a respectable candidate, since the allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller remains contested and I ranked it seventh. I also accept your argument that agreement between atomic-structure theory and measurement makes B042 an unusually clean case, which comes close to my own criterion of quantitative theory tied to experiment. I would still put B019 first, but I would not choose it over B042 if the committee concludes the moire pairing physics is too unsettled.

uncertainties: Whether eight years is enough to separate the robust phenomenology from the unsettled pairing mechanism for the citation.
Whether the committee can justify omitting Yuan Cao and other early experimental groups from a three-person allocation; my recollection of the history is not independently verified.
Whether the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction should be weighed against earlier twist-angle continuum-model work by Lopes dos Santos and colleagues.
Whether a two-part prize pairing B019 with a more mature candidate would be preferable to a single-achievement prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for the credited people on B019, B058 or B042. My only connection to the field is that I work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism, so I should defer to colleagues on atomic clocks and on the AMO and particle candidates.
